"'''Low'''" is the debut single by American rapper and singer [[Flo Rida]] featuring fellow American rapper and singer [[T-Pain]], Written by both alongside [[DJ Montay]], who produced it with the latter, it is the lead single from the former's debut album ''[[Mail on Sunday (album)|Mail on Sunday]]'' and the opening track of the [[Step Up 2: The Streets (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] to the 2008 film ''[[Step Up 2: The Streets]]''.

The song was a massive success worldwide and was the longest-running number-one single of 2008 in the United States, spending ten consecutive weeks atop the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. With over seven million digital downloads, it has been certified Diamond by the [[Recording Industry Association of America|RIAA]], and was the most downloaded single of [[2000s in music|the 2000s decade]], measured by paid digital downloads.<ref name="eruweb">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurweb.com/story/eur58242.cfm|title=FLO RIDA HAS DECADE'S TOP-SELLING DIGITAL SONG: 'Low' claims more than 5 million downloads.|work=EURweb|access-date=December 23, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113155753/http://www.eurweb.com/story/eur58242.cfm|archive-date=January 13, 2010}}</ref> The song was named third on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 Songs of the Decade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~dtompkin/music/list/Chart25.html|title=Charts – Billboard}}</ref> An official remix was made which also features [[Pitbull (rapper)|Pitbull]].

The song received two nominations at the [[51st Annual Grammy Awards]]: [[Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance|Best Rap/Sung Collaboration]] and [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Song|Best Rap Song]].

"Low" is the debut single by American rapper and singer Flo Rida featuring fellow American rapper and singer T-Pain, Written by both alongside DJ Montay, who produced it with the latter, it is the lead single from the former's debut album Mail on Sunday and the opening track of the soundtrack to the 2008 film Step Up 2: The Streets.

The song was a massive success worldwide and was the longest-running number-one single of 2008 in the United States, spending ten consecutive weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100. With over seven million digital downloads, it has been certified Diamond by the RIAA, and was the most downloaded single of the 2000s decade, measured by paid digital downloads. The song was named third on the Billboard Hot 100 Songs of the Decade. An official remix was made which also features Pitbull.

The song received two nominations at the 51st Annual Grammy Awards: Best Rap/Sung Collaboration and Best Rap Song.

T-Pain) |url=https://stereogum.com/2218733/the-number-ones-flo-ridas-low-feat-t-pain/columns/the-number-ones/ |access-date=February 28, 2026 |website=[[Stereogum]]}}</ref> It has a [[verse–chorus form]] while the melody is an [[Arpeggio|arpeggiated]] [[ostinato]] note sequence instead of a [[chord progression]]. T-Pain's rely heavily on synthesizers, with him using [[Auto-Tune]] and [[Call and response (music)|call and answer]] during the [[Song structure#Chorus or refrain|chorus]]. The song is written in the key of [[E-flat minor|E♭ minor]]. Set in the time signature of common time, it has a moderate [[tempo]] of 128 [[beats per minute]]. T-Pain's vocal range spans nearly two octaves from B♭<sub>2</sub> to F{{music|#}}<sub>4</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2008 |title=Flo Rida "Low" Sheet Music in Eb Minor (transporable) |url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/flo-rida/low/MN0063024 |access-date=February 28, 2026 |website=Musicnotes |publisher=[[Universal Music Publishing Group]]}}</ref>

"Low" has been described as a danceable hip-hop song, but more specifically crunk and Miami bass. The song features an Eurohouse aesthetic with 808 drum machines such as kick, sub bass, cymbals and handclaps. It has a verse–chorus form while the melody is an arpeggiated ostinato note sequence instead of a chord progression. T-Pain's rely heavily on synthesizers, with him using Auto-Tune and call and answer during the chorus. The song is written in the key of E♭ minor. Set in the time signature of common time, it has a moderate tempo of 128 beats per minute. T-Pain's vocal range spans nearly two octaves from B♭<sub>2</sub> to F{{music|#}}<sub>4</sub>.

Lyrically, the song describes a sexually desirable girl dancing in a club, and the singer's efforts to hook up with her, primarily by flaunting displays of cash. The girl is described in the chorus as wearing "Apple Bottom jeans" and "boots with the fur".

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
The song debuted at number 91 on the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for the week of November 6, 2007, and reached number 1 for the week of December 30, 2007.<ref name="acharts">[http://acharts.us/song/29058 "Flo Rida and T-Pain – Low worldwide chart positions and trajectories"]. ''aCharts.us''. Retrieved December 28, 2007.</ref> The song stayed on the Hot 100 for thirty-nine weeks before dropping out in June 2008.<ref name="Billboard">{{Cite magazine |url=http://billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003741823 |title=Danity Kane Snags Second Straight No. 1 Album |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=March 26, 2008 |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017194521/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/news/article_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1003741823 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

"Low" held the top position longer than any song did in 2008 (see [[List of Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles of 2008|List of ''Billboard'' Hot 100 number-one singles of 2008]]), and was the longest-running Hot 100 number 1 single since [[Beyoncé]]'s "[[Irreplaceable]]".<ref name="billboard chart beat">{{cite magazine|url=http://billboard.com/bbcom/chart_beat/bonus.jsp |title=In Depth Music Chart Analysis- Billboard.com- Search for Hot Ringtones |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=February 24, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090520053315/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/chart_beat/bonus.jsp |archive-date=May 20, 2009 }}''The long and short of it''. Retrieved February 14, 2008.</ref> The song is also the longest-running number 1 single in the history of the ''Billboard'' Digital Songs chart, topping the chart for thirteen weeks, and also on the now-defunct [[Pop 100]] chart, where it ruled for twelve weeks.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite magazine|url=http://billboard.com/bbcom/chart_beat/bonus.jsp |title=In Depth Music Chart Analysis- Billboard.com- Search for Hot Ringtones |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=February 24, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090520053315/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/chart_beat/bonus.jsp |archive-date=May 20, 2009}}''Lower and lowest''. Retrieved February 7, 2008.</ref> For the week of June 29, 2008, it became the first song ever to sell four million digital copies in the US,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-extra-thank-you-daniel-powter.html |title=Chart Watch Extra: Thank You, Daniel Powter |author=Paul Grein |work=Yahoo Music (Chart Watch) |date=January 7, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121003063301/http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-extra-thank-you-daniel-powter.html |archive-date=October 3, 2012}}</ref> and then for the week of June 21, 2009, the first to sell over five million copies.<ref name=":0" /> It was best-selling digitally-downloaded song until it was surpassed by [[the Black Eyed Peas]]' "[[I Gotta Feeling]]" in May 2010.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/black-eyed-peas-i-gotta-feeling-named-bestselling-digital-track-20100503 |title=Black Eyed Peas' "I Gotta Feeling" Named Bestselling Digital Track |author=Daniel Kreps |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=May 3, 2010 }}</ref> The song sold over six million in digital sales by August 7, 2011,<ref name=":2" /> and reached its seven millionth sales mark in sales in June 2014.<ref name="US_sales">{{cite web|last=Grein|first=Paul|url=https://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-rude-summer-hit-top-10-214615906.html|title=Chart Watch: 'Rude,' 'Summer' Hit Top 10|publisher=Yahoo Music|date=June 4, 2014|access-date=June 5, 2014}}</ref>

The physical release of the single occurred in the UK for the week of March 24, 2008. For the week of July 20, 2008, the song moved up to number 19 on the [[UK Singles Chart]], several months after its official release. It spent seventy-five weeks on the chart.<ref name="hot 100">{{cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/search/singles/Ever%20Fallin%20In%20Love|title=The Official Charts Company – Low by Flo Rida|website=[[OfficialCharts.com]]|access-date=February 16, 2008}}</ref> As of January 2012, the song has sold 613,434 copies in the UK.<ref name="Jones">{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Alan|title=Official Chart Analysis: Sales slow, but Sheeran and Cover Drive reign|url=http://www.musicweek.com/story.asp?sectioncode=1&storycode=1048325&c=1|work=[[Music Week]]|access-date=February 2, 2012|date=January 30, 2012}}</ref>

The song was ranked at number 26 on ''Billboard''{{'s}} All Time Hot 100.<ref name=":1" /> The song was also ranked the number 1 song for 2008 in ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'}}s ranking of the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2008|''Billboard'' Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2008]]. For the week of December 28, 2008, it was listed at number 11 on the UK Singles Chart year-end countdown and was named the highest-selling single in Australia in 2008. The song was a hit in Europe, reaching the Top 10 in Finland, Denmark and Belgium, and the Top 40 in Germany, Hungary, Norway and France.
sections.text:
The song debuted at number 91 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 for the week of November 6, 2007, and reached number 1 for the week of December 30, 2007. The song stayed on the Hot 100 for thirty-nine weeks before dropping out in June 2008.

"Low" held the top position longer than any song did in 2008 (see List of Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles of 2008), and was the longest-running Hot 100 number 1 single since Beyoncé's "Irreplaceable". The song is also the longest-running number 1 single in the history of the Billboard Digital Songs chart, topping the chart for thirteen weeks, and also on the now-defunct Pop 100 chart, where it ruled for twelve weeks. For the week of June 29, 2008, it became the first song ever to sell four million digital copies in the US, and then for the week of June 21, 2009, the first to sell over five million copies. It was best-selling digitally-downloaded song until it was surpassed by the Black Eyed Peas' "I Gotta Feeling" in May 2010. The song sold over six million in digital sales by August 7, 2011, and reached its seven millionth sales mark in sales in June 2014.

The physical release of the single occurred in the UK for the week of March 24, 2008. For the week of July 20, 2008, the song moved up to number 19 on the UK Singles Chart, several months after its official release. It spent seventy-five weeks on the chart. As of January 2012, the song has sold 613,434 copies in the UK.

The song was ranked at number 26 on Billboard{{'s}} All Time Hot 100. The song was also ranked the number 1 song for 2008 in Billboard{{'}}s ranking of the Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2008. For the week of December 28, 2008, it was listed at number 11 on the UK Singles Chart year-end countdown and was named the highest-selling single in Australia in 2008. The song was a hit in Europe, reaching the Top 10 in Finland, Denmark and Belgium, and the Top 40 in Germany, Hungary, Norway and France.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video of "Low" was directed by Bernard Gourley and contains certain clips from ''[[Step Up 2: The Streets]]''. It also contains cameos from [[Rick Ross]], [[DJ Khaled]], [[Cool & Dre]], [[Briana Evigan]], [[Torch (American rapper)|Torch]] and [[Gunplay (rapper)|Gunplay]] of [[Triple C's]] and [[Jermaine Dupri]]. Also, [[T-Pain]] and [[Flo Rida]] are in a nightclub in a few scenes. The music video reached the top spot on ''[[MTV Jams]]'' for five days, and for twenty-two days on ''[[Total Request Live|TRL]]''. The music video was also nominated at the [[2008 MTV Video Music Awards]] for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Male Video|Best Male Video]] and [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Hip-Hop Video|Best Hip-Hop Video]], but lost to [[Hurricane Chris (rapper)|Hurricane Chris]]' "[[Playas Rock]]" (Best Male Video) and [[Birdman (rapper)|Birdman]]'s "[[Pop Bottles]]" (Best Hip-Hop Video) music videos.
sections.text: The music video of "Low" was directed by Bernard Gourley and contains certain clips from Step Up 2: The Streets. It also contains cameos from Rick Ross, DJ Khaled, Cool & Dre, Briana Evigan, Torch and Gunplay of Triple C's and Jermaine Dupri. Also, T-Pain and Flo Rida are in a nightclub in a few scenes. The music video reached the top spot on MTV Jams for five days, and for twenty-two days on TRL. The music video was also nominated at the 2008 MTV Video Music Awards for Best Male Video and Best Hip-Hop Video, but lost to Hurricane Chris' "Playas Rock" (Best Male Video) and Birdman's "Pop Bottles" (Best Hip-Hop Video) music videos.

sections.heading: Certifications
Cover versions and media usage
sections.wikitext:
In 2020, the American grocery chain [[Kroger]] and their subsidiary stores began to use the song's chorus for a series of animated ads, highlighting coupons and low prices.

At the start of 2021, the ads became a minor [[Internet meme]] with user-generated [[YouTube]] and [[TikTok]] remixes.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.winsightgrocerybusiness.com/retailers/krojis-go-viral-kroger-low-ads-become-memes|title=Krojis Go Viral as Kroger 'Low' Ads Become Memes|last=Springer|first=Jon|date=February 3, 2021|work=Winsightgrocerybusiness.com|access-date=February 4, 2021}}</ref>

A parody of the song highlighting price drop was used in the 2021 [[Lazada]] 11.11 TV commercial featuring K-Pop boy group [[Seventeen (South Korean band)|Seventeen]] in the [[ASEAN]] region, where it was sung in [[Indonesian language|Indonesian]], [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]], [[Thai language|Thai]], [[Vietnamese language|Vietnamese]], and [[English language|English]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mb.com.ph/2021/10/13/lazada-welcomes-leading-k-pop-superstars-seventeen-as-first-regional-happiness-ambassador/?amp|title=Lazada welcomes leading K-pop superstars SEVENTEEN as first regional Happiness Ambassador – Manila Bulletin|website=Mb.com.ph|date=October 13, 2021 |access-date=December 28, 2021}}</ref>

In 2026, Dutch DJ [[Hardwell]] released a reworked version of the song in collaboration with [[Dr Phunk]] and [[Azteck]], through his label [[Revealed Recordings]]. The version retains elements of the original composition while featuring newly recorded vocals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DXzN4xER6WT/ |title=Hardwell, Dr Phunk & Azteck – Instagram post |website=Instagram |access-date=May 1, 2026}}</ref>
sections.text:
In 2020, the American grocery chain Kroger and their subsidiary stores began to use the song's chorus for a series of animated ads, highlighting coupons and low prices.

At the start of 2021, the ads became a minor Internet meme with user-generated YouTube and TikTok remixes.

A parody of the song highlighting price drop was used in the 2021 Lazada 11.11 TV commercial featuring K-Pop boy group Seventeen in the ASEAN region, where it was sung in Indonesian, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese, and English.

In 2026, Dutch DJ Hardwell released a reworked version of the song in collaboration with Dr Phunk and Azteck, through his label Revealed Recordings. The version retains elements of the original composition while featuring newly recorded vocals.
